reservoir_contract_note: What is universal across equipment is the boundary balance dE_r = P_in - P_out - P_loss. The state, constitutive law, capacity, losses, limits and upstream dynamics are equipment-specific. Every account implemented here has losses=null, i.e. it realises the LOSSLESS special case dE_r = P_in - P_out. Capacities are 1000 pu.s for the governor and exciter accounts and a class default of 1000 pu.s for the converter accounts, which the IEEE39 converter cases scale with rating (10 x Sn of the replaced machine: 3000 / 7000 / 8000 pu.s); these are accounting conventions, and reservoir magnitudes must NOT be ranked across component types on that basis.
reservoir_correction_note: 2026-09-25: every reservoir uses the constant-POWER inflow law dx_r = (P_ref - P_draw)/p_r, p_r = max(x_r/C, 1e-6), x_r(0) = p* C. Then p_r dx_r = P_ref - P_draw exactly, the reservoir is neutral (d(dx_r)/dx_r = 0 at equilibrium) and H_r(t) = H_r(0) - D_r(t) with the reservoir work D_r = int (P_draw - P_ref) dt, independent of C. The original constant-VOLUME law dx_r = P_ref/p* - P_draw/p_r had the unstable eigenvalue P_ref/(C p*^2); the converters used the stiff law dx = P_ref - P_draw with x(0) = 0, whose energy did not drain by exactly P_draw. One-way coupling is unchanged, so every plant trajectory is unchanged.
